name: Ontario: public health coverage for newcomers
name_fr: Ontario : assurance maladie publique pour les nouveaux arrivants
description: Who is covered by Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) by immigration status, any waiting period for newcomers, how to apply, the public drug-coverage model and the share of adults with a regular health care provider.

attributes.legal_status: in force (eligibility rules as published on the access date)

eligibility_by_status.citizen: Eligible as a resident (residency and presence rules apply).
eligibility_by_status.permanent_resident: Eligible (permanent residents; also applicants for PR whose application has not been denied), subject to living in Ontario as primary residence and 153 days' presence in any 12 months.
eligibility_by_status.work_permit_holder: Eligible if working full-time for an Ontario employer for at least 6 months (spouse and dependants may also qualify); live-in caregivers and seasonal agricultural workers with valid permits also listed.
eligibility_by_status.study_permit_holder: International students are not listed among eligible groups on the OHIP page; contact ServiceOntario.
eligibility_by_status.visitor: Not eligible (visitors and tourists are excluded from every provincial plan reviewed).

attributes.status_dependency: Which rule applies depends on the user's immigration status, which is unknown (USER-PROFILE.md: 'Citizenship(s) and current country of residence', 'Existing Canadian status or application').

newcomer_waiting_period.arriving_from_outside_canada: None — 'There is no longer a waiting period for OHIP coverage' (page updated 21 July 2025).

attributes.how_to_apply: In person at a ServiceOntario centre with the registration form and three original documents (status, Ontario residency, identity).
attributes.drug_coverage_model: Ontario Drug Benefit for residents 65+, social-assistance recipients and children/youth 24 and under without private coverage (OHIP+); $100 deductible for higher-income seniors; Trillium Drug Program for high costs relative to income (PMPRB 2020/21 summary).

regular_provider.source: CIHI indicator 'Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider', Statistics Canada CCHS

sources.title: Apply for OHIP and get a health card (updated 21 July 2025)
Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider — indicator data table (data updated October 2026); underlying data: Statistics Canada, Canadian Community Health Survey, Annual Component
sources.methodology: Weighted percent of adults 18+ reporting a regular/primary health care provider (family doctor, nurse practitioner or other); 95% confidence interval given. 2025 adult questions were harmonized, so compare with earlier years with caution.

sources.title: Public Drug Plan Designs, 2021/22 edition (describes 2020/21 plan designs; page modified 2024-01-30)

verification.notes: Provincial page(s) fetched directly where status is 'verified'; otherwise some content came from search-engine extracts of official pages (403 or bot-check on fetch). Regular-provider figures parsed from CIHI's published data table.

limitations: Eligibility text summarises official pages and is not legal advice; temporary-status rules change often. Drug-plan designs are from PMPRB's 2020/21 summary and may be out of date. 'Without a regular provider' is 100 minus the CIHI share (simple arithmetic).
